title: Definition, Nature and Scope of Psychology
summary: Psychology as the scientific study of behaviour and mental processes; its etymology (psyche + logos); the five-stage evolution of its subject matter; its nature as science, social science, natural science, applied science and dynamic discipline; scope, fields and applications.

notes.t: Psychology is the scientific study of behaviour and mental processes. The word comes from two Greek roots: psyche, meaning soul or mind, and logos, meaning study or science. Literally, psychology means 'the study of the soul.'

The scientific study of behaviour and mental processes. Behaviour covers all observable actions (actions, reactions, speech, gestures); mental processes are internal, subjective experiences (thoughts, feelings, perceptions, memories) that are inferred rather than directly observed.

Behaviour includes everything a person does that can be observed — actions, reactions, speech and gestures. Mental processes are internal, subjective experiences — thoughts, feelings, perceptions and memories — that cannot be directly observed but can be inferred from behaviour and self-report.

Psychology is best understood as several things at once: a science (systematic, empirical methods; testable and falsifiable hypotheses), a social science (people in social and cultural contexts), a natural science (biological bases of behaviour — brain, nervous system, hormones), an applied science (findings applied to clinical, educational, organisational and social problems) and a dynamic discipline (definition and methods have changed as the field matured).

notes.c: Major fields of psychology, focus and typical applications
r: Assessment, diagnosis and treatment of mental disorders
Milder emotional and adjustment problems; career and life guidance
Learning, teaching, curriculum, motivation, classroom environment
Workplace behaviour, selection, training, leadership, motivation
Group behaviour, attitudes, prejudice, conformity, leadership
Growth and change across the lifespan
Brain, nervous system, hormones, genetics and behaviour

notes.t: Behaviour is observable; mental processes are internal and inferred. The subject matter evolved: soul → mind → consciousness → behaviour → behaviour and mental processes. 1879 (Wundt, Leipzig) is the conventional birth-date of psychology as an experimental science.
